input.passage: In the 1840s, many reformers in Britain argued that the spread of cheap gas lighting would lengthen factory workdays, since employers could now keep machines running well after dark. Historian Ruth Calder's study of mill records from Lancashire suggests that this fear was only partly realized. Some mills did add evening shifts in the first years after installing gas lamps. ______ by the 1850s, most of those same mills had returned to daytime-only schedules, as the cost of fuel and the higher rate of accidents at night made the extra hours unprofitable.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
input.explanation: 앞 문장은 일부 공장이 초기에 야간 근무를 추가했다는 점(개혁가들의 우려가 일부 실현됨)을 인정하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 1850년대에 그 공장들이 다시 주간 근무로 돌아갔다고 말하므로 양보 후 반전 관계다. 따라서 대조와 시간 경과를 함께 나타내는 D가 정답이다. A는 야간 근무 추가가 주간 근무 복귀의 원인인 것처럼 만들지만, 복귀의 원인은 연료비와 사고로 제시되어 있다. B는 두 사실이 같은 방향의 유사한 사례라고 잘못 표시하며, C는 뒤 문장이 앞 문장을 재진술한다고 하지만 실제로는 반대 결과를 제시한다.
input.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank admits that some mills did add evening shifts at first, so the reformers' fear came partly true. The sentence after the blank says that by the 1850s those mills had gone back to daytime-only schedules. This is a concession followed by a reversal, so you need a transition that shows both contrast and the passage of time, which makes D correct. A treats the evening shifts as the cause of the return to daytime work, but the text gives fuel costs and accidents as the reasons. B wrongly presents the two facts as similar examples that point the same way, and C wrongly treats the second sentence as a restatement of the first, when it actually describes the opposite outcome.
input.design: There is no contrast word in the passage, so students must see the concession and reversal on their own ("only partly realized" → added shifts → later abandoned). A and C may tempt students who skim the text as one continuous narrative.

input.passage: Ecologists long assumed that the bright orange coloration of the rough-skinned newt warned predators of the potent toxin in its skin. Garter snakes in parts of the Pacific Northwest, however, have evolved resistance to that toxin and regularly eat the newts. Biologist Edmund Brodie III found that in these regions, newt populations carry far higher toxin levels than populations elsewhere. ______ the snakes' resistance appears not to have ended the newts' chemical defense but to have intensified it, with each species driving further change in the other.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
input.explanation: 마지막 문장은 앞 문장의 관찰(저항성 뱀이 있는 지역의 영원 독성이 더 높음)이 무엇을 뜻하는지 다시 풀어 해석하므로 재진술의 A가 정답이다. B는 '그런데도'라는 대조를 나타내는데, 뱀의 저항성과 영원의 방어가 대립처럼 보여 끌리지만 마지막 문장은 앞 문장과 반대되는 내용이 아니라 그 결과를 해석한 것이다. C는 구체적 사례를 들 때 쓰는데, 마지막 문장은 앞 문장보다 오히려 더 일반적인 해석이다. D는 별개의 비슷한 현상을 덧붙일 때 쓰지만 여기서는 같은 현상을 다시 설명하고 있다.
input.explanation_en: The last sentence restates and interprets the finding in the previous sentence: newts that live alongside resistant snakes have more toxin. That makes A, a restatement transition, the best choice. B signals contrast, and it can be tempting because snake resistance and newt defense seem to work against each other. But the last sentence doesn't contradict the previous one; it explains what that finding means. C would introduce a specific example, but the last sentence is a broader interpretation, not a more specific case. D would add a separate, similar point, but the sentence is describing the same phenomenon again in different words.
input.design: 빈칸 앞의 '저항성'과 '방어'가 대립처럼 보여 훑어 읽으면 B를 고르게 했다. 마지막 문장이 앞의 관찰을 해석한 재진술이라는 점을 알아차려야 A를 고를 수 있다.

input.passage: When engineers at a Dutch firm designed a pedestrian bridge from 3D-printed stainless steel, critics predicted that the printed metal would be too porous and brittle to bear heavy foot traffic. Early test samples did show tiny internal voids, and some layers bonded unevenly. ______ load tests on the finished twelve-meter span revealed that it could support several times the weight of a dense crowd without measurable deformation, and the bridge was installed over an Amsterdam canal.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
input.explanation: 앞 문장은 시험 샘플에서 내부 기공과 불균일한 접합이 나타났다는, 비평가들의 우려를 일부 뒷받침하는 사실을 인정한다. 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그런 결함이 있었는데도 완성된 다리가 큰 하중을 견뎠다는 결과를 제시하므로, 양보 후 반전을 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 결함이 뛰어난 강도의 원인처럼 만들어 인과 방향이 맞지 않는다. C는 뒤 문장이 결함을 구체적으로 설명하는 것처럼 만들지만, 실제로는 완성된 다리의 시험 결과라는 새로운 정보를 제시한다. D는 결함과 강도가 서로 비슷한 사례인 것처럼 연결하지만, 두 내용은 서로 대조된다.
input.explanation_en: The previous sentence admits that early samples had voids and uneven bonding, which partly supports what the critics feared. The next sentence reports that the finished bridge held very heavy loads despite those flaws, so the text needs a transition that admits a point and then reverses it. That makes A correct. B would mean the flaws caused the bridge's strength, which gets the cause and effect wrong. C would make the next sentence a specific detail about the flaws, but it actually gives new information: test results for the finished bridge. D presents the flaws and the strength as similar examples, but the two ideas contrast.
input.design: 빈칸 앞에 비평가 쪽을 뒷받침하는 결함 사실을 두어, 훑어 읽으면 인과 관계나 구체화로 오해하기 쉽게 했다. 정답을 고르려면 반전 관계를 정확히 파악해야 한다.

input.passage: Many desert plants survive drought by storing water in thick, fleshy tissues, a strategy familiar from cacti and agaves. The resurrection plant Selaginella lepidophylla, native to the Chihuahuan Desert, takes a very different approach. During dry spells, it lets almost all of its water evaporate, curling its fronds into a tight brown ball that appears dead. ______ when rain returns, the plant unfurls and resumes photosynthesis within hours, its cells having been protected throughout by sugars that stabilize membranes in the absence of water.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
input.explanation: 앞 문장은 식물이 물을 거의 다 잃고 '죽은 것처럼 보인다'고 말하고, 뒤 문장은 비가 오면 몇 시간 만에 다시 살아난다고 말한다. 이처럼 겉보기와 실제가 대비되므로 대조를 나타내는 B가 정답이다. A는 건조해진 상태가 회복의 원인처럼 보이게 만드는데, 실제로 회복의 원인은 비와 세포를 보호하는 당이므로 인과 방향이 맞지 않는다. C는 두 문장이 비슷한 내용을 말한다고 보지만, 둥글게 말려 죽은 듯한 모습과 다시 펼쳐지는 모습은 비슷하지 않고 반대이다. D는 뒤 문장을 앞 문장의 예시로 보지만, 비가 와서 회복하는 것은 건조기에 웅크리는 것의 사례가 아니다.
input.explanation_en: The previous sentence says the plant loses nearly all its water and "appears dead." The next sentence says it revives within hours once rain returns. Because the plant looks dead but is actually still alive, the sentences contrast, so B is correct. A makes the drying-out sound like the cause of the recovery, but the plant actually recovers because of the rain and the protective sugars, so the cause-and-effect direction is wrong. C says the two sentences describe something similar, but curling into a dead-looking ball and unfurling to grow again are opposites. D treats the next sentence as an example of the previous one, but reviving after rain is not an instance of curling up during drought.
input.design: There is no "but" or "however" in the passage to signal the contrast. Students have to notice the gap between "appears dead" and the plant's quick revival. A tempts readers who see a time sequence (drying, then reviving), and D tempts readers who connect the sugars to the plant's strategy.

input.passage: Along the coast of Bangladesh, engineers long assumed that building tall embankments around low-lying "polders" would protect farmland from tidal flooding. The embankments did keep seawater out during ordinary high tides. ______ by blocking the sediment that tides once spread across the land, they caused the enclosed fields to sink gradually relative to the rivers outside, so that when an embankment finally breached, water poured in deeper and stayed longer than before.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
input.explanation: 앞 문장은 제방이 평상시 만조에는 바닷물을 막았다는 긍정적 효과를 인정하고, 뒤 문장은 같은 제방이 퇴적물을 막아 땅을 가라앉게 해 결국 홍수 피해를 키웠다는 반대 결과를 제시하므로 '양보 후 반전'과 점진적 시간 경과를 함께 나타내는 C가 정답이다. A는 제방이 퇴적물을 막은 것이 원인이 된 것은 맞지만, 바닷물을 막은 것의 '결과'로 지반 침하가 일어난 것이 아니므로 인과 방향이 맞지 않는다. B는 뒤 문장이 앞 문장의 성공 사례를 보여 주는 예시가 아니라 그와 상반된 결과이므로 틀리다. D는 두 문장이 비슷한 효과를 말한다고 보지만, 실제로는 보호 효과와 피해 악화가 대조되므로 틀리다.
input.explanation_en: The previous sentence grants a benefit: the embankments kept seawater out during ordinary high tides. The next sentence then shows that the same embankments slowly made flooding worse by starving the land of sediment. This is a concession followed by a reversal that develops gradually, so C is correct. A may look tempting because the embankments did cause the sinking, but the sinking was not a result of keeping out the tides, which is what the previous sentence describes. B is wrong because the second sentence isn't an example of the success the passage just described; it contradicts it. D is wrong because the two sentences describe opposite effects, not similar ones.
input.design: There is no contrast word to give the answer away. Students must notice that the passage first grants a benefit and then reveals a harmful long-term effect. The wrong answer "As a result" is partly supported, since the embankments really did cause the sinking, so the student has to check the direction of cause and effect to rule it out.

input.passage: In Margaret Vell's novel The Lamplighter's Daughter (2019), the narrator, Hester, spends the first half of the book insisting that she has no interest in her late father's unfinished letters, which she keeps locked in a drawer she claims never to open. Vell, writing in the long, formal sentences of a Victorian novel, lets Hester repeat this claim in nearly every chapter. ______ the reader gradually notices that Hester can quote whole passages of the letters from memory, a detail that quietly exposes her indifference as a pose.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
input.explanation: 앞 문장은 Hester가 편지에 관심이 없다고 계속 주장한다는 내용이고, 뒤 문장은 그 주장이 반복되는 동안 독자가 그녀가 편지를 외우고 있음을 알아차린다는, 주장과 어긋나는 사실을 제시한다. 따라서 주장이 이어지는 '그 동안 내내' 반대 증거가 쌓인다는 대조적 동시성을 나타내는 B가 적절하다. A는 결과 관계를 나타내지만, 주장을 반복한다고 해서 그녀가 편지를 외우게 되는 것은 아니다. C는 뒤 문장이 앞 문장의 사례라는 뜻인데, 편지를 외운다는 것은 무관심을 주장하는 사례가 아니라 그 주장과 반대된다. D는 다시 말하기를 나타내지만, 뒤 문장은 앞 내용을 바꿔 말하는 것이 아니라 그것을 뒤집는다.
input.explanation_en: The previous sentence says Hester keeps claiming she has no interest in the letters. The next sentence reveals something that contradicts that claim: she can quote them from memory, and the reader notices this while she keeps repeating the claim. Choice B fits because "All the while" shows that this contradicting evidence builds up during the same stretch in which she makes her claims. Choice A signals a result, but repeating the claim doesn't cause her to know the letters by heart. Choice C would make the memorized passages an example of her claimed indifference, when they actually undercut it. Choice D signals a restatement, but the second sentence reverses the first point rather than rephrasing it.
input.design: 무관심 주장과 그 주장을 뒤집는 증거의 대조적 동시성을 어휘 단서 없이 판단하게 했다. 결과(A), 예시(C), 재진술(D)은 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯해 보이도록 배치했다.

input.passage: In her 2021 novel The Lamplighter's Ledger, Imogen Varley borrows the trappings of Victorian fiction: a foggy market town, a disputed inheritance, and a narrator who addresses the "gentle reader" directly. Early reviewers praised the book as a faithful revival of the nineteenth-century form. ______ Varley repeatedly undercuts that form, ending chapters not with the cliffhangers her models favored but with the narrator admitting she has invented the scene just described.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
input.explanation: 앞 문장은 평론가들이 이 소설을 19세기 형식의 '충실한 부활'로 칭찬했다고 하고, 뒤 문장은 작가가 그 형식을 반복적으로 무너뜨린다고 말하므로 대조 관계이며 D가 정답이다. A는 두 문장이 같은 방향의 내용이라고 보지만 실제로는 서로 상반된다. B는 평론가들의 칭찬 때문에 작가가 형식을 무너뜨렸다는 인과 관계를 만드는데, 소설은 서평보다 먼저 쓰였으므로 논리에 맞지 않는다. C는 뒤 문장이 '충실한 부활'의 예시라고 보지만, 장 끝에서 장면을 지어냈다고 고백하는 것은 오히려 그 평가를 반박하는 내용이다.
input.explanation_en: The previous sentence says reviewers praised the novel as a faithful revival of the nineteenth-century form, while the next sentence says Varley repeatedly undercuts that form, so the relationship is contrast and D is correct. A treats the two sentences as making similar points, but they actually point in opposite directions. B suggests that the reviewers' praise caused Varley to undercut the form, which makes no sense because the novel was written before it was reviewed. C presents the next sentence as an example of a faithful revival, but a narrator admitting she invented a scene challenges that judgment rather than illustrating it.
input.design: 빈칸 앞에 칭찬, 뒤에 형식을 무너뜨린다는 내용을 두어, 학생이 두 문장의 의미를 직접 비교해야 대조 관계를 알 수 있게 했다. 오답 C와 A는 두 문장이 모두 Victorian form을 다룬다는 표면적 연결을 이용한 함정이고, B는 시간 순서 때문에 배제된다.

input.passage: When engineers in the Netherlands began testing roads paved with recycled plastic modules in 2018, critics predicted that the hollow, lightweight blocks would crack under the weight of heavy traffic. Early pilot sections, laid on bicycle paths in Zwolle, were deliberately limited to light loads so that this concern could be studied before wider use. ______ the modules' most valuable feature turned out to have little to do with strength at all: their hollow interiors could store rainwater during storms and release it slowly, easing pressure on the city's drainage system.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
input.explanation: 앞 문장들은 비평가와 시험 설계가 모두 '강도(균열)' 문제에 초점을 맞췄다는 내용이고, 마지막 문장은 가장 가치 있는 특징이 강도와 무관한 빗물 저장 기능으로 드러났다는 예상 밖의 반전이다. 따라서 기대와 다른 실제 결과를 제시하는 B가 정답이다. A는 가벼운 하중으로 제한한 결과 빗물 저장 기능이 드러났다는 인과 관계를 만드는데, 하중 제한이 그 발견의 원인이 아니므로 틀린다. C는 마지막 문장을 강도 우려의 한 예시로 만들지만 그 내용은 강도와 무관하다. D는 앞 내용과 비슷한 점을 덧붙이는 것으로 만들지만 마지막 문장은 앞의 초점과 대조된다.
input.explanation_en: The earlier sentences show that critics and the test design both focused on strength, meaning whether the blocks would crack. The last sentence brings an unexpected turn: the blocks' most valuable feature had nothing to do with strength and was instead about storing rainwater. Choice B fits because it introduces an actual result that differs from what people expected. Choice A suggests that limiting the loads caused the rainwater discovery, but nothing in the text links the two. Choice C would make the last sentence an example of the strength concern, yet it is about something other than strength. Choice D signals a similar point, but the last sentence contrasts with the earlier focus instead of matching it.
input.design: Both A (the order of events seems to suggest cause and effect) and D (it adds one more fact about the modules) seem plausible at first. Only a careful reader notices the shift from the expected concern about strength to an unexpected benefit, which calls for a transition showing contrast.

input.passage: In her 2019 novel The Lamplighter's Ledger, Imogen Varley adopts many trappings of the nineteenth-century triple-decker: an omniscient narrator, a sprawling cast of provincial families, and chapters that end on carefully timed revelations. Reviewers who expected a nostalgic pastiche, however, found something less comfortable. Varley's narrator repeatedly interrupts the plot to admit that she cannot know what her characters privately feel, and she even revises earlier descriptions when new evidence emerges. ______ the very device that once guaranteed Victorian readers a stable moral vantage point becomes, in Varley's hands, a source of doubt.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
input.explanation: 마지막 문장은 앞 문장에서 묘사한 서술자의 행동(내면을 알 수 없다고 인정하고, 앞선 묘사를 고침)이 낳는 결과를 요약한다. 즉 전지적 서술자라는 장치가 확실성 대신 의심을 낳게 된다는 것이므로 '이런 방식으로'라는 뜻의 C가 가장 논리적이다. A는 대조를 나타내지만 마지막 문장은 앞 내용을 뒤집지 않고 그대로 이어받는다. 지문의 'however'에 끌려 고르기 쉬운 오답이다. B는 구체적인 예를 들 때 쓰지만 마지막 문장은 앞의 구체적 사례를 일반화한 내용이다. D는 비슷한 다른 사례를 덧붙일 때 쓰지만 마지막 문장은 새로운 사례가 아니라 같은 현상의 의미를 설명한다.
input.explanation_en: The final sentence sums up what the narrator's behavior in the previous sentence leads to. Because she admits she can't know her characters' feelings and revises her earlier descriptions, the omniscient narrator ends up creating doubt instead of certainty. That makes C ("In this way,") the most logical choice. A signals contrast, but the last sentence builds on the previous point rather than reversing it. The "however" earlier in the text makes A tempting. B introduces a specific example, but the last sentence moves in the opposite direction, from specific details to a general point. D adds a parallel case, but the last sentence doesn't bring in a new case. It explains what the same behavior means.
input.design: This item has no vocabulary clue. To get it right, students have to see that the specific details lead to a general conclusion (the result of the narrator's behavior). Students who skim may pick A because of the earlier "however," or B or D because they misread how the sentences relate.

input.passage: Along the coast of Bangladesh, villagers have long built earthen embankments to keep tidal floods out of low-lying farmland. The walls succeeded in protecting crops, but they also blocked the sediment that tides once spread across the land each season. Over decades, the enclosed fields slowly sank while riverbeds outside the walls rose with trapped silt. ______ some embanked areas now sit below the level of the surrounding channels, so that when a wall breaches, water pours in and can remain for months.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
input.explanation: 앞 문장은 제방 안 농지는 가라앉고 바깥 하천 바닥은 높아졌다고 설명하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 결과 일부 지역이 주변 수로보다 낮아져 제방이 무너지면 물이 몇 달간 고인다고 말한다. 따라서 원인-결과를 잇는 D가 정답이다. A는 지문 앞부분의 '보호 성공 vs 퇴적물 차단'이라는 대조에 이끌린 오답이지만, 빈칸 뒤 내용은 앞 문장과 상반되지 않고 그로부터 따라 나온다. B는 뒤 문장이 구체적 사례처럼 보이지만, 앞 문장을 예시하는 것이 아니라 그 결과로 생긴 새로운 상황을 제시한다. C는 '안쪽 농지 vs 바깥 하천'의 대비가 앞 문장 안에 있을 뿐, 두 문장 사이의 관계는 대조가 아니다.
input.explanation_en: The previous sentence explains that the fields inside the walls sank while the riverbeds outside rose. The sentence after the blank gives what followed from that: some embanked areas now sit lower than the nearby channels, so floodwater stays for months after a breach. That is a cause-and-effect relationship, so D is correct. A might pull you in because the passage earlier contrasts protecting crops with blocking sediment, but the final sentence doesn't push against the one before it. It follows directly from it. B is wrong because the final sentence isn't an example of sinking land. It describes a new situation that the sinking caused. C picks up on the inside-versus-outside contrast within the previous sentence, but the two sentences themselves aren't being contrasted.
input.design: There are no vocabulary cues here. The reader has to see that the final sentence is the result of the previous one. The tempting wrong answers come from the contrast earlier in the passage and within the previous sentence (A, C) and from the specific feel of the final sentence (B).

input.passage: Ecologists long assumed that the bright orange coloration of the monarch-mimicking viceroy butterfly offered protection only because birds confused it with the toxic monarch. Experiments by Jane Brower and later David Ritland complicated this picture: when birds were fed viceroys alone, many rejected them after a single taste, suggesting the viceroy is itself distasteful. ______ the viceroy's resemblance to the monarch is now understood less as a harmless species borrowing another's reputation and more as two unpalatable species reinforcing a shared warning signal.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
input.explanation: 앞 문장은 바이스로이 나비 자체가 맛이 없다는 실험 결과를 제시하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 결과로 두 나비의 유사성에 대한 해석이 바뀌었다는 결론을 말하므로 원인-결과 관계인 C(Accordingly)가 적절하다. A(Nevertheless)는 기존 가정과 실험 결과 사이의 대조에 끌리게 하지만, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 실험 결과와 상반되지 않고 그 결과를 따른다. B(For example)는 뒤 문장이 앞 결과의 구체적 사례가 아니라 그 결과에서 나온 일반적 재해석이므로 맞지 않는다. D(Similarly)는 두 종이 비슷하다는 내용에 끌릴 수 있지만, 앞 문장과 유사한 별개의 사실을 덧붙이는 것이 아니므로 오답이다.
input.explanation_en: The previous sentence reports experimental evidence that the viceroy is itself distasteful, and the sentence after the blank gives the revised interpretation that follows from that evidence, so the cause-and-effect transition in C (Accordingly) is the best fit. A (Nevertheless) may tempt you because the experiments contradict the old assumption, but the final sentence builds on the experimental result instead of contradicting it. B (For example) doesn't work because the final sentence is not a specific case of the finding; it is a broader conclusion drawn from it. D (Similarly) may seem fitting because the passage is about two butterflies that look alike, but the final sentence does not add a separate, parallel fact.
input.design: 빈칸 앞의 '기존 가정 vs 실험'이라는 대조와 '유사성'이라는 소재가 A와 D를 끌어당기게 했다. 빈칸 앞뒤 문장이 증거와 결론의 관계임을 확인해야 C를 고를 수 있다.

input.passage: When the first public lending libraries opened in English mill towns in the 1850s, reformers predicted that factory workers would flock to them for books on science and self-improvement. Borrowing records from towns such as Bolton and Salford tell a different story. Most loans were novels, travel narratives, and serialized adventure stories, and technical manuals often sat on the shelves for years without being checked out. ______ the reformers' hopes were not entirely misplaced: library registers show that many workers who first came in for fiction later borrowed history and geography titles, suggesting that reading for pleasure gradually led some patrons toward the very subjects reformers had promoted.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
input.explanation: 앞 문장들은 대출 기록이 개혁가들의 예측과 달랐다(주로 소설 대출)고 말하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그럼에도 개혁가들의 기대가 완전히 틀린 것은 아니었다고 일부 되돌린다. 따라서 앞 내용을 인정하면서 반전시키는 A가 정답이다. B는 소설 위주 대출이 '결과적으로' 기대가 맞았다는 인과를 만들어 논리가 뒤집힌다. 뒤 문장에 '소설이 역사로 이어졌다'는 인과 내용이 있어 그럴듯해 보이지만, 빈칸은 앞 문장과의 관계를 나타내야 한다. C는 뒤 문장이 앞의 주장(기대와 다름)의 사례가 아니므로 틀리고, D는 두 문장이 같은 방향의 내용이 아니므로 틀리다.
input.explanation_en: The earlier sentences show that borrowing records contradicted the reformers' predictions, since most loans were novels. The sentence after the blank partly takes that back by saying the hopes were "not entirely misplaced," so you need a transition that admits the previous point and then turns against it. That makes A correct. B might look tempting because the final sentence describes fiction leading to history reading, but "As a result" would claim that the mostly-fiction borrowing caused the reformers' hopes to be valid, which isn't the logic connecting the two sentences. C is wrong because the sentence is not an example of workers ignoring serious books, and D is wrong because the sentence doesn't make a parallel point in the same direction.
input.design: 빈칸 앞뒤의 관계는 어휘 단서 없이 '예측 실패 → 부분적 회복'이라는 양보 후 반전 논리로만 드러나게 했다. 뒤 문장 속 인과 내용이 B를, 구체적 기록 언급이 C를 그럴듯하게 만들도록 설계했다.

input.passage: Many species of freshwater mussel depend on fish to complete their life cycle: the mussel larvae clamp onto a host fish's gills and ride along for several weeks before dropping off to settle in the riverbed. Ecologist Wendell Haag and colleagues found that in stretches of river where dams had blocked the movement of host fish, mussel populations were dominated by older adults, with almost no juveniles present. ______ the researchers concluded that many of these populations, though they appear stable in surveys of living animals, are not replacing themselves and may eventually disappear.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
input.explanation: 앞 문장은 댐으로 숙주 어류의 이동이 막힌 구간에서 어린 개체가 거의 없다는 관찰 결과를 제시하고, 뒤 문장은 그 관찰을 근거로 개체군이 스스로 대체되지 못해 사라질 수 있다는 결론을 내린다. 따라서 관찰에서 결론으로 이어지는 결과 관계를 나타내는 D가 정답이다. A는 뒤 문장의 '안정적으로 보이지만'이라는 양보 표현에 끌린 오답으로, 결론은 관찰과 대조되지 않고 그 관찰에서 도출된다. B는 뒤 문장을 앞 내용의 구체적 사례로 만드는데, 실제로는 더 일반적인 결론이다. C는 단순한 재진술을 나타내지만, 뒤 문장은 개체군 소멸 가능성이라는 새로운 추론을 덧붙인다.
input.explanation_en: The previous sentence gives an observation: where dams blocked host fish, mussel populations had almost no juveniles. The next sentence draws a conclusion from that observation: the populations aren't replacing themselves and may disappear. Since the conclusion follows from the evidence, D is correct. A is tempting because of the contrast phrase "though they appear stable," but the conclusion doesn't oppose the observation; it builds on it. B would make the conclusion an example of the observation, but the conclusion is actually broader. C signals a simple restatement, but the final sentence adds a new inference about possible disappearance.
input.design: 문장 내부의 양보절(though…stable)이 Nevertheless를 유도하고, 결론이 관찰을 일부 다시 말하는 듯해 In other words도 그럴듯하게 만들었다. 두 문장의 관계가 관찰에서 추론으로 이어진다는 점을 따져야 정답을 고를 수 있다.

input.passage: In Hollis Varga's 2019 novel The Lamplighter's Ledger, the narrator, a retired clerk in a fog-bound port town, describes his neighbors with the elaborate courtesy of a Victorian gentleman, praising their "admirable thrift" and "steadfast devotion to propriety." Readers who take these compliments at face value may find the narrator merely old-fashioned. ______ the details he records alongside his praise, such as a widow's locked pantry while her servants go hungry, reveal that his elegant phrases are quietly working as accusations.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
input.explanation: 앞 문장은 칭찬을 액면 그대로 받아들이는 독자에게는 화자가 그저 구식으로 보일 수 있다고 인정하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 실제로는 그 칭찬이 비난으로 작동한다고 뒤집으므로 양보 후 반전을 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 '구식으로 보임'이 '비난이 드러남'의 원인이 아니므로 인과 방향이 맞지 않는다. C는 뒤 문장의 과부 사례 때문에 예시처럼 보이지만, 그 사례는 앞 문장의 '구식' 해석을 보여 주는 것이 아니라 그 해석을 반박한다. D는 두 문장이 같은 주장을 하는 것이 아니라 서로 대립하므로 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The previous sentence grants that readers who take the compliments literally may see the narrator as merely old-fashioned. The next sentence overturns that reading by showing that his praise actually works as accusation, so this is a concession followed by a reversal, and A is correct. B suggests that seeming old-fashioned causes the accusations to come out, but that cause-and-effect link doesn't hold. C may be tempting because the widow's pantry is a specific detail, but that detail argues against the "old-fashioned" reading instead of illustrating it. D doesn't work because the two sentences contradict each other instead of making similar points.
input.design: 명시적 대조 어휘 없이 '액면 그대로의 해석'과 '실제 기능'이라는 양보-반전 구조로 만들었다. 뒤 문장의 구체적 사례가 For example을, 앞뒤 흐름이 Consequently를 그럴듯하게 보이게 한다.

input.passage: When British railway companies adopted a single standardized "railway time" in the 1840s, many towns resisted, preferring to keep clocks set by the local position of the sun. Some town halls even displayed two minute hands, one for local time and one for London time. ______ by 1855 the great majority of public clocks in Great Britain had been set to Greenwich Mean Time, a shift driven less by legislation than by the practical demands of catching trains.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
input.design: 'However' 같은 어휘 단서 없이 저항(양보) 후 결국 채택(반전)이라는 논리를 파악해야 한다. 'Consequently'는 철도 도입이 원인처럼 보이게 하고, 'For example'·'Similarly'는 시계 관련 사례가 이어져 겉보기에 그럴듯한 함정이 되도록 설계했다.
input.explanation: 앞 문장들은 여러 도시가 철도 시간에 저항하며 지역 시간을 고수했다고 설명하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그럼에도 1855년경에는 대부분의 시계가 그리니치 표준시로 맞춰졌다고 말한다. 저항이 있었는데도 결국 채택되었다는 양보-반전 관계이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 철도 시간이 결국 채택된 원인처럼 보여 그럴듯하지만, 바로 앞 문장(시계에 분침 두 개를 단 저항 사례)이 그 결과로 이어지지 않으므로 맞지 않는다. C는 빈칸 뒤 문장을 저항의 예시로 만들지만, 이 문장은 저항이 아니라 채택을 보여 준다. D는 유사성을 나타내지만 두 내용은 서로 반대된다.
input.explanation_en: The earlier sentences say that many towns resisted railway time and kept their local time. The sentence after the blank says that by 1855 most clocks had switched to Greenwich Mean Time anyway. That is a concession followed by a reversal: the towns resisted, yet they adopted it in the end, so B is correct. A might look reasonable because the railways did eventually cause the change, but the sentence right before the blank describes resistance (town clocks with two minute hands), and the switch does not follow from that resistance as a result. C would make the final sentence an example of resistance, but it actually describes adoption. D signals that the two ideas are alike, but they are opposites.

input.passage: Along the coast of Bangladesh, rivers carry roughly a billion tons of sediment to the sea each year, and some of that material settles in the delta, slowly building up new land. Planners once assumed that this natural deposition would be enough to offset rising sea levels across the region. ______ geographer Leila Haque found that embankments built in the 1960s to protect farmland have blocked sediment from reaching many enclosed islands, which have consequently sunk by up to a meter relative to nearby unprotected land.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
input.explanation: 앞 문장은 계획가들이 퇴적만으로 해수면 상승을 상쇄할 수 있다고 '가정했다'는 내용이고, 뒤 문장은 제방이 퇴적을 막아 섬들이 오히려 가라앉았다는 연구 결과로 그 가정을 뒤집는다. 따라서 대조를 나타내는 B가 정답이다. A는 결과 관계를 나타내지만, 섬의 침하는 그 가정에서 따라 나온 결과가 아니라 가정에 반하는 증거이다. C는 뒤 문장을 구체적 사례로 보이게 하지만, 그 연구는 가정을 뒷받침하는 사례가 아니라 반박하는 내용이다. D는 비슷한 내용을 덧붙일 때 쓰는데, 두 문장은 서로 같은 방향의 주장이 아니다.
input.explanation_en: The previous sentence describes what planners once assumed: that sediment deposition alone would offset sea-level rise. The next sentence presents research showing that embankments blocked sediment and the islands actually sank, which contradicts that assumption. So the contrast transition in B is correct. A signals a result, but the sinking doesn't follow from the assumption; it is evidence against it. C would present the study as an instance supporting the assumption, when the study actually challenges it. D signals that a similar point is being added, but the two sentences point in opposite directions.
input.design: 'once assumed'가 앞으로 반박이 나올 것을 암시하지만, 이를 놓치고 겉보기에 이어지는 퇴적·섬 이야기만 훑어 읽으면 예시나 인과 관계로 착각하기 쉽게 설계했다.

input.passage: When engineers in the Netherlands designed the Maeslantkering, a storm-surge barrier protecting the port of Rotterdam, they faced an unusual constraint: the barrier could not obstruct one of the busiest shipping channels in Europe. A permanent wall across the waterway was therefore out of the question. ______ the engineers built two enormous hinged gates, each roughly as long as the Eiffel Tower is tall, that rest in dry docks along the banks and swing shut only when forecasts predict a dangerous surge.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
input.explanation: 앞 문장은 항로를 막는 영구적인 벽이 불가능하다고 하여 한 가지 해결책을 배제하고, 뒤 문장은 그 대신 채택된 해결책(평소에는 강둑에 보관하다가 필요할 때만 닫히는 수문)을 제시한다. 따라서 배제된 대안을 대체하는 관계이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 '그럼에도 불구하고'라는 뜻이라 벽을 짓지 못했는데도 벽을 지었다는 식의 양보가 되어야 하지만, 수문은 그 제약을 따른 결과이지 제약에 반하는 행동이 아니다. B는 두 가지 비슷한 사례를 나란히 놓을 때 쓰는데, 수문은 영구 벽과 비슷한 것이 아니라 그와 대조되는 방식이다. D는 뒤 문장을 앞 문장의 예시로 만들지만, 수문은 '영구적인 벽'의 사례가 아니라 그것을 대신하는 방안이다.
input.explanation_en: The previous sentence rules out one solution, a permanent wall across the waterway, and the next sentence describes the solution the engineers used in its place: gates that are stored on the banks and close only when needed. Because the text swaps a rejected option for a chosen one, C is correct. A ("Nevertheless") would mean the engineers acted despite the constraint, but the movable gates follow the constraint rather than go against it. B treats the gates as similar to something already mentioned, but they are the opposite of a permanent wall. D presents the next sentence as an example of the previous claim, but the gates are not an example of a permanent wall. They are a replacement for it.
input.design: 빈칸 앞은 해결책을 배제하고 빈칸 뒤는 대체 해결책을 제시하므로 대체 관계를 추론해야 한다. 'out of the question'을 대충 읽은 학생은 반전으로 보아 A를 고르기 쉽고, 뒤 문장이 구체적인 내용이라 D(예시)도 그럴듯해 보이도록 설계했다.

input.passage: When gas streetlamps spread through European cities in the early nineteenth century, many reformers predicted that brighter streets would chiefly reduce nighttime crime. Historian Joachim Schlör has argued that the lamps' most lasting effect was different: by making evening streets feel navigable, they encouraged shopkeepers, theaters, and cafés to extend their hours. ______ the nightly rhythms of urban commerce and leisure, rather than crime rates, were what the new lighting most visibly transformed.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
input.explanation: 마지막 문장은 앞 문장에서 말한 내용, 즉 가로등의 주된 효과가 범죄 감소가 아니라 상점·극장·카페의 영업시간 연장이었다는 점을 더 일반적인 말로 다시 정리한다. 따라서 바꾸어 말하기를 나타내는 C가 정답이다. A는 '범죄 감소'라는 예측과 대비되는 느낌 때문에 그럴듯해 보이지만, 그 대비는 이미 앞 문장에 나와 있고 마지막 문장은 앞 문장을 반박하지 않는다. B는 마지막 문장이 구체적인 사례가 아니라 앞 내용을 요약한 일반 진술이므로 맞지 않는다. D는 앞 문장과 비슷한 별개의 현상을 새로 덧붙이는 것이 아니므로 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The last sentence restates the previous one in more general terms. The lamps' main effect was longer hours for shops, theaters, and cafés, not lower crime, and that is the same as saying the lamps changed the nightly rhythms of commerce and leisure. Because the sentence repeats an idea in different words, C is the correct answer. A might seem right because there is a contrast with the reformers' prediction about crime, but that contrast was already made in the previous sentence, and the final sentence agrees with Schlör's point rather than going against it. B doesn't work because the final sentence is a general summary, not a specific example. D doesn't work because the final sentence doesn't add a separate but similar development.
input.design: 'rather than crime rates'라는 대비 표현 때문에 대충 읽으면 A를 고르게 되지만, 꼼꼼히 읽으면 마지막 문장이 앞 문장을 바꾸어 말한 것임을 알 수 있다. B와 D도 각각 구체화와 추가 관계로 일부 그럴듯하게 만들었다.

input.passage: When engineers in the Netherlands began testing roads paved with a porous asphalt mix, they expected the main benefit to be drainage: rainwater seeps through tiny gaps in the surface rather than pooling on top, reducing spray and hydroplaning. ______ the same network of gaps turned out to absorb much of the sound produced where tires meet pavement, and drivers on test stretches reported noticeably quieter rides even on dry days.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
input.design: 'expected the main benefit'라는 기대와, 같은 구조가 의도치 않게 소음을 줄였다는 부가 발견을 연결해야 한다. 인과(A), 대조(B), 재진술(C)이 각각 부분적으로 그럴듯하게 보이도록 구성했다.
input.explanation: 첫 문장은 엔지니어들이 배수를 주된 이점으로 '예상했다'고 하고, 둘째 문장은 같은 틈새 구조가 소음까지 흡수한다는 사실이 '드러났다'(turned out)고 한다. 이는 예상하지 못한 추가 발견이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 소음 감소가 배수 효과의 결과처럼 보이게 만들지만, 소음 감소는 배수가 아니라 틈새 구조 자체에서 생기며 맑은 날에도 나타난다. B는 앞 내용과 어긋나는 반전을 나타내지만, 소음 감소는 배수 이점을 부정하지 않고 그 위에 더해지는 효과이다. C는 재진술을 나타내는데, 소음은 배수와 다른 새로운 정보이다.
input.explanation_en: The first sentence says engineers expected drainage to be the main benefit, and the second says the same gaps "turned out" to absorb tire noise. That is a surprising extra discovery, so D is correct. A makes the noise reduction sound like a result of drainage, but the quieter ride comes from the gaps themselves and happens even on dry days. B signals a reversal, but the noise benefit adds to the drainage benefit rather than working against it. C signals a restatement, but noise is new information, not drainage described in other words.

Because Heringer trained local workers to build the METI School, those workers could apply its improved earth-building methods to their own homes—an effect on local practice that critics see as the building's main achievement.
The METI School uses rice straw mixed with rammed earth, a technique local builders already knew, along with bamboo harvested near the village.

input.explanation: 목표는 비평가들이 이 학교를 외관 이상으로 평가하는 '이유'를 설명하는 것이다. B는 현지 노동자 교육과 그 방법의 재사용(메모 4)을 비평가들의 평가(메모 5)와 연결해 이유를 명확히 제시한다. A와 C는 재료와 공법을 정확히 소개하지만 비평가의 평가나 그 이유는 언급하지 않는다. D는 비평가를 언급하지만 대나무 구조만 덧붙일 뿐 왜 외관 이상으로 평가받는지 설명하지 못한다.
input.explanation_en: The goal is to explain why critics value the school for more than how it looks. B links the training of local workers and their reuse of the methods (note 4) to the critics' view that this effect on local practice is the main achievement (note 5), so it gives a clear reason. A and C accurately describe the materials and techniques, but they never mention critics or explain why the building is valued. D mentions critics, but it only adds a detail about the bamboo frame and does not explain why they value the building beyond its appearance.
input.design: To get this right, students must connect two notes: the worker training (cause) and the critics' judgment (evaluation). Each distractor uses accurate notes, and D even mentions critics, so a student skimming for that word could be misled.

input.passage: Many species of reef-building coral depend on symbiotic algae living inside their tissues, and when ocean temperatures rise, corals often expel these algae and turn white, a process known as bleaching. Marine biologist Hollie Putnam and colleagues examined whether some corals might survive such events by feeding more heavily on plankton. They found that colonies of the coral Montipora capitata that increased their plankton intake during bleaching lost far less body mass than colonies that did not. ______ the ability to switch food sources may help explain why certain coral species recover from bleaching more quickly than others.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
input.explanation: 마지막 문장은 앞 문장의 연구 결과(백화 중 플랑크톤 섭취를 늘린 산호가 체질량을 덜 잃음)에서 도출되는 결론(먹이 전환 능력이 회복 속도 차이를 설명할 수 있음)이므로 결과·결론을 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 대조·양보를 나타내지만, 마지막 문장은 앞 내용을 뒤집지 않고 그대로 이어받는다. C는 구체적 사례를 제시하는 표현인데, 마지막 문장은 앞 문장보다 더 일반적인 주장이므로 방향이 반대이다. D는 두 대상을 비교할 때 쓰지만, 마지막 문장은 새로운 비교 대상을 제시하는 것이 아니라 앞의 발견에서 추론을 끌어낸다.
input.explanation_en: The last sentence draws a conclusion from the finding before it: corals that ate more plankton during bleaching lost less mass, so the ability to switch food sources may explain why some species recover faster. That makes A, a transition showing a result or conclusion, the best choice. B signals contrast or concession, but the final sentence builds on the finding rather than going against it. C introduces a specific example, but the final sentence is more general than the study it follows, so the direction is reversed. D sets up a comparison between two things, but the final sentence draws an inference from the study instead of presenting something new to compare.
input.design: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 '연구 결과 → 일반적 함의'라는 논리에서만 도출되게 했다. 'certain coral species ... than others'라는 표현이 비교(D)를 끌어들이고, 연구 사례와 일반 진술이 함께 있어 예시(C)도 그럴듯해 보이도록 설계했다.

input.passage:

- She did not begin studying botany until 1921, when she was over 50 years old.
- Over the next 13 years, she collected roughly 145,000 plant specimens across Mexico and South America.
- About 500 of the species she collected were new to science.
- Around 50 of those new species were named in her honor, such as Mimosa mexiae.
input.question: The student wants to emphasize how productive Mexía was despite starting her career late in life. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Ynés Mexía, a Mexican American botanical collector, gathered about 500 species that were new to science, around 50 of which were named in her honor.
Ynés Mexía, who began studying botany in 1921, was honored when roughly 50 plant species, including Mimosa mexiae, were named after her.
Although Ynés Mexía did not begin studying botany until she was over 50, she went on to collect roughly 145,000 plant specimens in just 13 years.
Ynés Mexía collected roughly 145,000 plant specimens across Mexico and South America, making her an important botanical collector of the early twentieth century.
input.explanation: 목표는 두 가지, 즉 '늦은 시작'과 '많은 성과'를 함께 보여 주는 것이다. C는 50세가 넘어 식물학을 시작했다는 점과 13년 동안 약 145,000점을 수집했다는 점을 'Although'로 연결해 이 둘을 모두 충족한다. A는 성과는 보여 주지만 늦게 시작했다는 점이 빠져 있다. B는 1921년이라는 연도만 제시할 뿐 나이를 밝히지 않아 '늦은 시작'이 드러나지 않고, 생산성보다 명예에 초점을 둔다. D는 수집량은 정확히 언급하지만 늦은 출발이라는 대비가 없다.
input.explanation_en: Your goal has two parts: you need to show that Mexía started late and that she was highly productive anyway. C does both. It says she started botany after age 50, and it uses "Although" to connect that fact to her roughly 145,000 specimens collected in just 13 years. A shows what she achieved but never mentions her late start. B gives only the year 1921, not her age, so it doesn't show that she started late, and it focuses on honors rather than productivity. D states her collection total correctly but leaves out the contrast with her late start.
input.design: B와 D는 정확한 메모(시작 연도, 수집량)를 쓰지만 목표의 한 축이 빠지도록 설계했다. 특히 B는 1921년만 제시하고 나이를 밝히지 않아, 훑어 읽으면 정답처럼 보이게 했다.

input.explanation: 목표는 플레어의 에너지 양을 '지속 시간'과 대비해 강조하는 것이므로 약 0.2초라는 짧은 시간과 태양 10만 년치 에너지라는 두 메모를 함께 써야 한다. D가 이 둘을 결합해 목표를 달성한다. A는 플레어 발생 사실과 거리만 제시하고 에너지 크기나 지속 시간을 다루지 않는다. B는 거리와 대기 영향으로 플레어의 강력함을 암시하지만 지속 시간 대비 에너지량을 보여주지 않는다. C는 마그네타의 일반적 특징을 설명할 뿐 2004년 플레어의 구체적 에너지와 시간을 언급하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: Your goal is to emphasize how much energy the flare released compared with how long it lasted, so you need both the duration (about two-tenths of a second) and the energy (more than the Sun emits in about 100,000 years). Choice D combines exactly those two notes, so it is the best answer. Choice A gives the flare's date and the magnetar's distance but says nothing about energy or duration. Choice B hints at the flare's power through its effect on Earth's atmosphere, but it doesn't contrast energy with duration. Choice C describes magnetars in general and never gives the 2004 flare's specific energy or brief duration.
input.design: B와 C는 플레어의 위력을 부분적으로 암시해 그럴듯하지만, '지속 시간 대비' 조건을 확인해야만 배제되도록 두 메모 결합을 요구했다.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In behavioral economics, "mental accounting" describes how people treat money differently depending on its source or intended use.
- Economist Richard Thaler popularized the concept in the 1980s.
- In one study, participants who received a $25 surprise gift card spent it on items they would not normally buy.
- The same participants, when handed $25 in cash from their own paychecks, mostly saved it or spent it on routine expenses.
- Standard economic theory assumes money is fungible: any dollar should be treated the same as any other dollar.
input.question: The student wants to emphasize how the study's findings challenge an assumption of standard economic theory. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Although standard theory holds that every dollar is interchangeable, participants spent a $25 gift card on unusual purchases while saving or routinely spending the same amount from their paychecks.
Popularized by Richard Thaler in the 1980s, mental accounting describes how people treat money differently depending on its source or intended use.
In one study, participants who received a $25 surprise gift card spent it on items they would not normally buy, while $25 in paycheck cash was mostly saved.
Standard economic theory assumes money is fungible, a principle that economist Richard Thaler examined when he popularized mental accounting in the 1980s.
input.explanation: 목표는 연구 결과가 표준 이론의 가정에 어떻게 도전하는지 강조하는 것이므로, '돈은 대체 가능하다'는 가정과 같은 25달러를 출처에 따라 다르게 쓴 결과를 대조해 연결해야 한다. A는 'Although'로 두 정보를 대비시켜 이 목표를 달성한다. B는 개념과 그 기원만 설명하고 연구나 가정은 언급하지 않는다. C는 연구 결과를 정확히 제시하지만 이것이 어떤 가정에 도전하는지는 밝히지 않는다. D는 가정과 Thaler를 언급하지만 연구 결과가 빠져 있어 도전의 근거가 드러나지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: Your goal is to show how the study's findings challenge an assumption, so the sentence needs both the fungibility assumption and the result that people treated the same $25 differently depending on where it came from. Choice A sets these side by side with "Although," so the contradiction is clear. Choice B only defines mental accounting and says where it came from, without mentioning the study or the assumption. Choice C reports the study accurately but never names the assumption the findings challenge. Choice D mentions the assumption and Thaler but leaves out the study's findings, so it never shows the challenge itself.
input.design: To answer correctly, students have to combine two notes: the fungibility assumption and the study's findings. Choice C gives the findings accurately, and choice D gives the assumption, but each leaves out the other half, so careful comparison is needed to rule them out.

input.passage:

Whereas Silbo Gomero whistlers use pitch to imitate the vowels and consonants of Spanish, Hmong whistlers use pitch to reproduce the tones that distinguish Hmong words.
Silbo Gomero, which whistles Spanish, can be understood up to about 5 kilometers away, while Hmong whistled speech is used in Southeast Asia.
Like Hmong, which uses pitch to tell words apart, Silbo Gomero relies on changes in pitch to convey spoken language through whistles.
input.explanation: 목표는 두 휘파람 언어가 말을 '표현하는 방식'의 차이를 강조하는 것이다. B는 Silbo Gomero가 음높이로 모음·자음을 흉내 내는 반면 Hmong은 단어를 구별하는 성조를 재현한다는 점을 대조해 목표를 정확히 달성한다. A는 두 언어의 공통점(장거리 소통)을 말하므로 차이를 강조하지 못한다. C는 '대조'의 형식을 갖췄지만 전달 거리와 지역을 비교할 뿐 표현 방식의 차이는 다루지 않는다. D는 두 언어 모두 음높이를 쓴다는 유사성을 강조하여 목표와 반대된다.
input.explanation_en: Your goal is to highlight a difference in how two whistled languages represent speech. B does this by contrasting Silbo Gomero, where pitch imitates Spanish vowels and consonants, with Hmong, where pitch reproduces the tones that distinguish words. A points out a similarity (long-distance communication), not a difference. C is set up as a contrast, but it compares range and location rather than how speech is represented. D stresses that both languages use pitch, which is a similarity and works against the goal.
input.design: To find the answer, the student has to combine notes 3 and 5 and see that the difference lies in how speech is represented. C has a contrast structure but differs on the wrong thing, and D uses the same notes but turns them into a similarity, so both require careful comparison.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

- In 1973, she proposed the "nearly neutral theory" of molecular evolution.
- Earlier, her mentor Motoo Kimura had argued that most genetic mutations are completely neutral, neither helping nor harming an organism.
- Ohta argued instead that many mutations are slightly harmful, with effects so small that chance can still determine whether they spread.

input.question: The student wants to emphasize how Ohta's theory differed from Kimura's view. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Tomoko Ohta, a Japanese population geneticist who studied under Motoo Kimura, received the Crafoord Prize in Biosciences in 2015.
Ohta's nearly neutral theory, proposed in 1973, predicts that slightly harmful mutations spread more easily in small populations than in large ones.
Both Kimura and Ohta studied molecular evolution, and in 1973 Ohta proposed a theory about how genetic mutations spread.

Whereas Kimura had argued that most mutations are completely neutral, Ohta proposed that many are slightly harmful, though too weakly for that harm to keep chance from determining whether they spread.
input.explanation: D는 Kimura의 견해(대부분의 돌연변이는 완전히 중립적이다)와 Ohta의 견해(많은 돌연변이가 약간 해롭다)를 'Whereas'로 직접 대비시키므로 두 이론의 차이를 강조한다는 목표를 달성한다. A는 두 사람의 사제 관계와 수상 사실만 언급할 뿐 이론의 차이는 다루지 않는다. B는 Ohta 이론의 정확한 예측을 담고 있지만 Kimura의 견해가 빠져 있어 대조가 이루어지지 않는다. C는 두 사람을 함께 언급하지만 공통점만 제시하고 무엇이 달랐는지는 밝히지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: D directly contrasts Kimura's view (most mutations are completely neutral) with Ohta's view (many mutations are slightly harmful) using "Whereas," so it emphasizes how the two theories differed. A mentions only their mentor-student relationship and Ohta's prize, not any difference in their ideas. B accurately states a prediction of Ohta's theory, but it leaves out Kimura's view, so there is no contrast. C names both scientists, but it points out only what they had in common and never says how their views differed.
